difficulties: None blocking. The entry reads MICM's own camp-data JSON, so the converter is a near one-to-one rename (products [name, yield] -> {"species","yield"}, label -> "MUSICA name", scaling_factor -> "scaling factor", M -> "parameterization": "air density", "rate units": "mol m-3", initial state without the canonical "environment"); emissions are USER_DEFINED reactions with "reactants": [], which the reader and generator accept. The Makefile hard-codes configs/ts1.json (no variable), so the file was swapped and restored (SHA-256 checked). Pitfall: macOS make 3.81 compares mtimes to the second, so a swap within the same second as the previous build is silently treated as up to date (seen twice in extra checks: one test build skipped, one timing build that relinked the generic program for the new mechanism but left the specialized program on the previous one). The scripts pause 2 s before each swap; every reported result comes from a build whose log shows all 8 mechanism-dependent targets rebuilt. make env downloaded the pinned packages from conda-forge (the prescribed setup). The entry's own generator test (tests/specialized.c, built for the TS1 slot by make bin/test_specialized_ts1) passes on chapman; on both CB5 variants its synthetic perturbed inputs make the generic and generated solvers both exceed 1000 steps with identical step and rejection counts (a test-input limitation, not a discrepancy). The retained tools/translate_ts1.py is TS1-only (asserts 210 species and 547 reactions), and the scenario driver treats only parameters whose names start with "j" as photolysis (TS1 naming; not used here).
generated_kernels_evidence: bin/ts1_bench_specialized is built with -DCH_SPECIALIZED, so tools/ts1_io.h:12-18 maps ch_update_rates and ch_solve to the generated ch_rates_ts1_specialized and ch_solve_ts1_specialized (tools/specialized_solver.h, included by the generated ts1_specialized.c with CH_FORCE/CH_JACOBIAN/CH_FACTOR/CH_LINEAR bound to generated functions). Each of the six generated dispatchers (rates, force, Jacobian, shift, factor, linear) tests "if (n == CH_DEFAULT_GROUP_SIZE && n % CH_KERNEL_WIDTH == 0)" (n = the group's cell count; the Makefile passes -DCH_DEFAULT_GROUP_SIZE=32 -DCH_KERNEL_WIDTH=32) and calls the generated *_fixed blocks (constant stride 32) or, otherwise, the generated runtime-stride blocks ts1_specialized_<kind>_kernel_<k>(n,...); there is no branch to the generic library's kernels. tools/ts1_bench.c:23 shrinks the group to the cell count when cells < 32. In the built binaries (otool -tV) each dispatcher is "cmp x22, #0x20; b.ne" to the runtime-stride blocks, and _ch_solve_ts1_specialized calls only the generated dispatchers/kernels plus the library's ch_normalized_error and ch_post_solve (and the step controller by pointer), never ch_force, ch_jacobian or ch_solve. No runtime trace: lldb needs developer mode, which is disabled on this machine.
